name: Strategy & Geopolitics
summary: AI is now treated as strategic infrastructure: chip controls swing between easing and tightening, states fund sovereign compute, militaries adopt AI-first plans, and power grids become a binding constraint.

regions.name: Compute, chips & export controls
regions.summary: The US opened case-by-case H200 sales to China in January 2026, yet shipments stalled; Blackwell stays barred and May guidance extended licence rules to Chinese firms' offshore units.
regions.whyItMatters: Who can buy frontier chips shapes which countries and companies can train and run the largest models.
regions.openQuestion: Will licensed H200 sales to China ever ship at scale, or do both governments now prefer decoupling?

landmarks.name: US opens case-by-case H200 sales to China
landmarks.summary: A BIS rule of 13 January moved H200-class chips to case-by-case licence review for China, with a 50% volume cap, US lab testing and certifications; a 25% chip tariff followed.

landmarks.name: Export enforcer: zero H200s sold to China
landmarks.summary: Commerce export enforcement chief David Peters told a House hearing on 24 February that, to his understanding, no H200s had yet gone to China.
landmarks.note: Bloomberg page is closed to scripts; supported by search snippet only.

landmarks.name: BIS targets Chinese firms' offshore units
landmarks.summary: Guidance posted on 31 May says advanced-chip licence rules cover China-headquartered entities located abroad; BIS called it a clarification of 2023 requirements, per Reuters.

deepDives.title: CNAS Insights: Unpacking the H200 Export Policy
deepDives.why: Think-tank analysis of what the January 2026 rule allows, its 50% cap and its weak points.

deepDives.title: Epoch AI: data on AI chip sales
deepDives.why: Open estimates of AI chip sales, compute and spending by chip type, updated regularly.

deepDives.why: Interactive map of who supplies each step of advanced chip production, from Georgetown's CSET.

deepDives.title: CSET: AI Chips: What They Are and Why They Matter
deepDives.why: Standard primer on why leading-edge chips matter for AI and for export control policy.

regions.name: US-China competition
regions.summary: China is building a domestic AI stack on local chips and open models. The May summit settled little, but Xi's September US visit extended the trade truce to January 2027 and set up an AI dialogue.
regions.whyItMatters: The two countries set the pace of frontier AI, and their rivalry drives chip rules, supply chains and model access worldwide.
regions.openQuestion: Can China's domestic chips sustain frontier training without Nvidia hardware?

landmarks.name: DeepSeek V4 tuned for Chinese chips
landmarks.summary: DeepSeek previewed V4-Pro and V4-Flash on 24 April; it reportedly optimised V4 for Huawei and Cambricon chips and gave Nvidia and AMD no early access.
landmarks.note: Chip detail is TNW relaying Reuters and The Information, not a DeepSeek statement.

landmarks.name: Trump-Xi Beijing summit
landmarks.summary: Trump left Beijing on 15 May after two days with few firm deals: no H200 breakthrough, no rare-earth resolution and no decision on extending the trade truce, per Reuters.

landmarks.name: China's 15th Five-Year Plan elevates AI+
landmarks.summary: The draft 2026-2030 plan sent to the National People's Congress in March mentions AI 52 times, up from 11, and makes the AI Plus initiative a top national priority.

landmarks.name: Xi's US visit: truce extended, AI dialogue
landmarks.summary: During Xi's 23-25 September state visit the two sides extended their trade truce to 10 January 2027 and agreed to set up a China-US dialogue on AI risks and benefits.
landmarks.note: Wikipedia summary citing Reuters and FT; the original reports are closed to scripts.

deepDives.title: ASPI Strategist: Key takeaways from China's Two Sessions
deepDives.why: Short analytical read on what the new five-year plan signals for technology and security.

deepDives.title: DigiChina (Stanford)
deepDives.why: Translations and expert readings of Chinese technology policy documents and speeches.

deepDives.why: Regular analysis and interviews on China, US technology policy and export controls.

deepDives.title: Wikipedia: China-United States trade war
deepDives.why: Dated timeline of tariffs, truces and export measures, with links to the news reports.

regions.name: National AI strategies & sovereign AI
regions.summary: Governments from Canada to the Gulf and EU are funding domestic compute and models to reduce dependence on foreign providers, often through deals with US chipmakers.
regions.whyItMatters: Public money and state deals now decide where large AI clusters get built and who controls them.
regions.openQuestion: Does sovereign AI built on imported US chips and cloud software deliver real independence?

landmarks.name: Canada's 'AI for All' strategy
landmarks.summary: Announced by Prime Minister Mark Carney on 4 June, the six-pillar strategy includes a sovereign AI foundation and continues more than C$2bn of existing compute investment.

landmarks.name: EU AI gigafactories tender
landmarks.summary: EuroHPC opened a call on 30 July to select consortia to build and run AI gigafactories; bids are due 3 December 2026 for Lot 2 and, after an extension, 4 February 2027 for Lot 1.

landmarks.name: Saudi Humain expands Nvidia deal
landmarks.summary: PIF-owned Humain announced 84MW of Nvidia capacity, about 27,000 GPUs, in two phases; the 70MW Vera Rubin phase planned from mid-2027 is subject to final agreements.

landmarks.name: US Genesis Mission for AI in science
landmarks.summary: Executive Order 14363, signed 24 November 2025, directs the Energy Department to build a shared AI platform for scientific discovery across the national labs.

deepDives.title: Canada's National Artificial Intelligence Strategy: AI for All
deepDives.why: The primary document: six pillars, targets and the sovereign compute plans.

deepDives.title: European Commission: AI Gigafactories
deepDives.why: Official page on the programme's aims, funding approach and timeline.

deepDives.why: Yearly data on AI laws, public investment and national strategies across countries.

deepDives.title: OECD.AI: national AI policies
deepDives.why: Searchable database of AI strategies and policy initiatives by country.

regions.name: International governance & safety institutes
regions.summary: Global AI governance has shifted to broad, nonbinding forums: the India summit, a new UN scientific panel and dialogue, and an annual international safety science report.
regions.whyItMatters: These forums are the only places where most governments, including the US and China, discuss AI risk together.
regions.openQuestion: Can nonbinding declarations and science panels constrain frontier developers, or only describe what they do?

landmarks.name: International AI Safety Report 2026
landmarks.summary: The second report, published in February and led by Yoshua Bengio with over 100 experts, finds pre-deployment tests often fail to predict how AI systems behave in real use.

landmarks.name: New Delhi Declaration at AI Impact Summit
landmarks.summary: The summit closed on 21 February with a declaration endorsed by 88 countries and organisations, including the US, UK, EU, China and Russia, built around voluntary frameworks.

landmarks.name: First UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance
landmarks.summary: The first Dialogue met in Geneva on 6-7 July, informed by the UN scientific panel's preliminary report; the second is set for New York on 3-4 May 2027.
landmarks.note: UN page is closed to scripts; dates rest on a search snippet from the earlier pass.

deepDives.title: International AI Safety Report 2026: extended summary
deepDives.why: The report's own 20-page policymaker summary of capabilities, risks and safeguards.

deepDives.why: Research centre publishing papers on international AI governance and frontier regulation.

regions.name: Defense & military AI
regions.summary: The Pentagon adopted an AI-first strategy and lost a first court ruling over its supply chain risk label for Anthropic, while Ukraine pushes battlefield AI but says full integration is years away.
regions.whyItMatters: Militaries are becoming major AI customers, and the terms they set test how far labs can restrict use of their models.
regions.openQuestion: Can an AI lab keep usage limits on its models once a government treats them as defence infrastructure?

landmarks.name: Pentagon AI Acceleration Strategy
landmarks.summary: Hegseth's January strategy aims for an 'AI-first' warfighting force, names seven pace-setting projects and orders 'any lawful use' language in AI contracts within 180 days.

landmarks.name: Court rules Anthropic risk label unlawful
landmarks.summary: A California federal judge ruled on 27 August that the Pentagon's supply chain risk label for Anthropic was unlawful retaliation; a second suit in Washington DC is still pending.

landmarks.name: Ukraine bets on battlefield AI
landmarks.summary: Defense AI Center head Danylo Tsvok told AP that AI is 'about our survival' and that a networked, AI-coordinated battlefield could arrive within three to five years.
landmarks.note: AP interview read on a member station's copy; AP's own site is closed to scripts.

deepDives.title: Release of the War Department's AI Acceleration Strategy
deepDives.why: The department's own release: three pillars and seven pace-setting projects.

deepDives.title: CSIS: Ukraine's Future Vision and Current Capabilities for Waging AI-Enabled Autonomous Warfare
deepDives.why: Detailed think-tank study of how Ukraine builds and fields military AI and autonomy.

deepDives.title: SIPRI: Artificial intelligence
deepDives.why: Research programme on military AI, autonomy and arms control, with reports and data.

regions.name: Energy & data centres
regions.summary: Data centre electricity use is forecast to rise about a quarter in 2026, pushing hyperscalers into nuclear deals and making grids such as PJM a constraint on AI buildout.
regions.whyItMatters: Power, not chips, is increasingly what limits how fast AI capacity can be added and who pays for it.
regions.openQuestion: Who bears the grid and bill costs if data centre demand forecasts prove too high, or too low?

landmarks.name: Gartner: data centre power up 26% in 2026
landmarks.summary: Gartner forecasts global data centre electricity use of 565TWh in 2026, up from 447TWh in 2025, driven by AI-optimised servers.
landmarks.note: Gartner page is closed to scripts; figures rest on a search snippet.

landmarks.name: Meta backs up to 6.6GW of nuclear power
landmarks.summary: Agreements announced on 9 January with Vistra, TerraPower and Oklo cover existing plants and planned advanced reactors; Meta says they support up to 6.6GW by 2035.

landmarks.name: BNEF: data centres a fifth of US power by 2035
landmarks.summary: BloombergNEF projects data centres at about 20% of US electricity use in 2035, up from 5.9% today and 12% in 2030, with above-average shares in the PJM and Texas grids.

landmarks.name: Epoch AI maps the largest AI data centres
landmarks.summary: Epoch AI's satellite and permit-based database, updated 6 November, covers 96 AI data centre sites with an estimated 15.1GW of IT power.

deepDives.title: IEA: Energy and AI
deepDives.why: The reference international study of data centre electricity demand and supply options.

deepDives.title: Epoch AI: data on AI data centres
deepDives.why: Open database of the largest AI data centres: power, compute and cost estimates per site.

deepDives.title: US DOE: report on electricity demand from data centres
deepDives.why: Government summary of the Berkeley Lab study projecting US data centre load to 2028.

deepDives.title: World Nuclear News: Meta announces agreements for new nuclear
deepDives.why: Industry-press detail on each deal: plants, megawatts and target dates.

regions.name: Elections & information integrity
regions.summary: The 2026 US midterms saw heavy spending on AI-generated political ads, mostly without disclaimers; rules are a patchwork of state labelling laws and few voters yet use chatbots.
regions.whyItMatters: Elections are the most visible test of whether synthetic media and chatbots change what voters believe.
regions.openQuestion: Did AI-generated ads and chatbot answers measurably shift votes, or mainly erode trust in what is real?

landmarks.name: AI-generated ads in US midterms
landmarks.summary: The Wesleyan Media Project counted 220 AI-generated ads with over $137m of spending by mid-October, 27% carrying a disclaimer; two weeks later it tracked 289 ads and $187m.

landmarks.name: State AI ad laws fail to ensure disclosure
landmarks.summary: AP reported that AI attack ads were common in the midterms and that candidates at times disregarded a patchwork of state disclosure laws.
landmarks.note: AP story read on a member newspaper's copy; AP's own site is closed to scripts.

landmarks.name: Few voters use chatbots for election info
landmarks.summary: A Pew survey of 5,273 US adults on 12-18 October found 8% using AI chatbots for 2026 election information: 11% of those under 50 and 4% of those older.

deepDives.title: Wesleyan Media Project: 2026 election releases
deepDives.why: Running reports on political ad spending, including counts of AI-generated ads.

deepDives.title: States United: How Well Do AI Platforms Answer Voter Questions?
deepDives.why: Tests of AI platforms' answers to practical voting questions before the midterms.

deepDives.title: Public Citizen: Tracker of State Legislation on Deepfakes in Elections
deepDives.why: State-by-state status of laws on deepfakes and AI disclosure in campaigns.

deepDives.title: Knight Institute: We Looked at 78 Election Deepfakes
deepDives.why: Sceptical analysis arguing that election misinformation is mostly not an AI problem.

regions.name: Open vs closed models
regions.summary: Chinese labs keep releasing strong open-weight models and are reported to lead open-model usage; Meta launched its Muse Spark model closed in April, then released a smaller open model in August.
regions.whyItMatters: Open weights decide who can run and adapt capable models without permission, including outside the US.
regions.openQuestion: Will US labs keep releasing competitive open weights, or cede that layer to Chinese developers?

landmarks.name: Meta launches closed Muse Spark
landmarks.summary: The first model from Meta Superintelligence Labs launched on 8 April through meta.ai and a private API preview, with no downloadable weights, a break from the Llama line.

landmarks.name: DeepSeek V4 released as open weights
landmarks.summary: DeepSeek released V4-Pro (1.6 trillion parameters) and V4-Flash as open weights on Hugging Face on 24 April, both with a one-million-token context window.

landmarks.name: Chinese models dominate open-weight usage
landmarks.summary: A Wing VC analysis of OpenRouter data puts Chinese open-weight models at about 61% of routed tokens by May 2026, with four of the five most-used models Chinese.
landmarks.note: Single VC analysis of OpenRouter data, not an official OpenRouter figure.

landmarks.name: MIT Tech Review on China's open-source bet
landmarks.summary: The article says Chinese labs win developers by making top models free, citing a study that put China at 17.1% of model downloads against 15.86% for the US.

landmarks.name: Meta releases open-weight Muse Glimmer
landmarks.summary: On 10 August Meta put the weights of Muse Glimmer, a smaller model based on its closed Spark 1.2, on Hugging Face for free; it can run on a single GPU.

deepDives.title: Open Source Initiative: The Open Source AI Definition
deepDives.why: The OSI's definition of what counts as open source AI, and why weights alone do not.

deepDives.why: US government report weighing the risks and benefits of open model weights.

deepDives.title: Interconnects AI
deepDives.why: Nathan Lambert's newsletter, with regular coverage of open models and their adoption.

regions.name: Domestic AI regulation
regions.summary: The EU's AI Omnibus pushed high-risk rules to 2027-28, while the White House moved to preempt state AI laws through litigation, funding conditions and a proposed federal framework.
regions.whyItMatters: These rules set the compliance burden for anyone building or deploying AI in the two largest Western markets.
regions.openQuestion: Will delay and preemption produce simpler rules, or a long gap with few binding rules at all?

landmarks.name: EU AI Omnibus delays high-risk rules
landmarks.summary: Agreed on 7 May and in force from 27 July, the AI Omnibus moves high-risk obligations to 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 and bans AI nudification apps from December 2026.

landmarks.name: US order targets state AI laws
landmarks.summary: Executive Order 14365 of 11 December 2025 orders a DOJ AI Litigation Task Force to challenge state AI laws and ties remaining BEAD broadband funds to states' AI rules.

landmarks.name: White House AI legislative framework
landmarks.summary: Released on 20 March, the framework asks Congress to act in seven areas, including preempting state AI laws it calls unduly burdensome while keeping child-protection laws.

landmarks.name: US order on frontier model security
landmarks.summary: Executive Order 14409 of 2 June sets up an AI cybersecurity clearinghouse and provides for government access to covered frontier models up to 30 days before wider release.
